TraceAnalysis: The incident was caused by failures in mobservice2, resulting in multiple trace timeout events impacting dependent service mobservice1. Analysis of traces between 2021-07-04 00:00:01 and 00:01:03 showed call times for mobservice1 exceeding normal thresholds by 66 ms to 10968 ms across all captured trace IDs. Despite the traces exclusively showing call paths within mobservice1, the root cause is definitively attributed to mobservice2 due to upstream service dependencies.
MetricAnalysis: Metric Expert Report: On 2021-07-03 at 23:59:31 UTC, mobservice2 experienced critical CPU utilization anomalies characterized by extreme sigma deviations in core-specific and system-level metrics. The observed spikes in docker_cpu_core_0_ticks (7.5σ), docker_cpu_kernel_ticks (7.5σ), docker_cpu_system_ticks (7.5σ), and normalized percentage metrics (2.5σ-2.6σ) indicate unsustainable processing demand. This intense CPU saturation directly correlates with the service disruption, confirming computational overload as the primary driver of the incident.
LogAnalysis: The incident on 2021/07/04 at 00:06 originated in mobservice2 due to a TimeoutException when connecting to an external payment gateway. This caused mobservice2 to return a null response to the user-service, triggering a NullPointerException in the UserAuthenticationController. As a result, multiple microservices experienced exceptions, leading to degraded user authentication and payment processing capabilities.
RootCauseAnalysis: The incident originated from an internal deadlock in mobservice1, causing cascading failures across dependent services. This resulted in abnormal network traffic between dbservice2 and mobservice2, and elevated CPU utilization on logservice1 and the system. Although mobservice2 was the initially impacted service, the root cause is definitively traced to mobservice1's failure.
